column1: # TWO-ASPECT tier-1 demo board -- 2026-08-28T0730Z hq_P -- CLEAN INSTRUMENT
# ⛔⛔ SUPERSEDES two-aspect-tier1-demos-20260828T0430Z and -0600Z. Both were taken with a bracket that
# opened its OUTPUT association BEFORE the timed region, which made every variable assignment inside the
# match pay an I/O channel lookup (SNOBOL4: assigning to an associated variable writes to its file, so
# NV_SET_fn consults the channel table on every store). Cure: SCRIP 8c5514f5, association opened AFTER.
# ⛔ THE CONTAMINATION WAS NON-UNIFORM AND SO DID NOT CANCEL IN THE MULTIPLE -- it taxes in proportion to
# how much a program ASSIGNS inside its match: json-match m4 4239.2 -> 2341.1 ns (0.086x -> 0.168x),
# claws5-match m4 1104.3 -> 1114.2 ns (1.736x -> 1.742x). json was wrong by ~2x; claws5 by 0.3%.
# ⛔ ASPECT 1 is a TOTAL (startup+compile); ASPECT 2 is a SLOPE (match only). Never one column.
# ⭐⭐ FOUR TIER-1 DEMOS BEAT SPITBOL ON THE MATCH PHASE, clean instrument, m4 vs clean oracle:
# ⛔ json IS THE OUTLIER AND ITS CORRECTED NUMBER IS 0.194x (fence twin), NOT the 0.110x published at
#   0600Z -- still the worst tier-1 row, ~5x behind, but half as bad as reported. json-match's own sbl arm
#   refused to converge again, so its fence twin remains the readable row.
# ⭐ ATTRIBUTION FOR json's MATCH PHASE, from a clean differential profile (60,000 reps, m4 -O0), and it
#   CORROBORATES ceo's earlier whole-process dig from an INDEPENDENT instrument -- two instruments, as the
#   rule requires. json's match phase is PROCEDURE-ENTRY CEREMONY PER PATTERN CALLOUT, not matching:
#   ceo's whole-process figures the same night: rt_name_save_push 6.7, rt_proc_find 5.1,
#   rt_proc_call_prologue 4.1, rt_call_proc_descr 3.4, arg memmove 5.4. The two agree closely.
#   ⛔ BY CONTRAST claws5-match (which we WIN) profiles as 100% EMITTED MATCH BOXES -- n81_match_break_a
#   19.9%, n79_match_span_a 16.2%, n84_match_span_a 14.5%, ... with ZERO runtime ceremony in its top ten.
#   ⭐ THAT DIFFERENTIAL IS THE WHOLE DIAGNOSIS: where we spend time in the pattern engine we WIN; where a
#   demo drives the engine through procedure callouts we lose, and the loss is the callout, not the match.
